column2: She brought her, and the goddess was divided in seven ways; and this Gautami Ganga went sevenfold to the sea.

Dharmashastras and whatever else rests on your word — what is greater than holy places, gifts, sacrifices, austerities, and service of deities and mantras? Tell me, lord.
brahmapuran:175:12	What you, revered one, say with devotion must be so and not otherwise.
brahmapuran:175:13	You ought to cut this doubt of mine by your word, Brahmin; having heard the desired inner thought, I have therefore come to wonder.

Listen, Narada; I shall tell the supreme secret dharma. Holy places are fourfold, and the yugas are as many;
brahmapuran:175:15	three qualities, three eternal gods, and the Vedas with the Smritis are declared four.
brahmapuran:175:16	The human aims are four, and speech is fourfold, and the qualities too, Narada, are four in equality.
brahmapuran:175:17	Everywhere dharma is common, since dharma is eternal; as means and end it is held to be of many kinds.
brahmapuran:175:18	Its support is twofold, place and time always; the dharma that depends on time always declines and grows.
brahmapuran:175:19	According to the yugas, one quarter of it declines, greatly wise one; the dependence on place is likewise of both.
brahmapuran:175:20	Dharma that depends on time is constantly established in place; when yugas decline, it does not decline in places.
brahmapuran:175:21	When it is lacking in both, there would be the absence of dharma; therefore dharma supported by place, four-footed, is well established.
brahmapuran:175:22	That dharma too stays in places in the form of holy places; in the Krita yuga dharma stands supporting place and time.
brahmapuran:175:23	In Treta, lacking a quarter, that quarter remains in place; in Dvapara half; dharma stands in place at the time.
brahmapuran:175:24	In Kali dharma moves in distress with one quarter. One who knows dharma of such kind does not lose it.
brahmapuran:175:25	By the influence of the yugas, distinctions of class are established; from the qualities and the doers of qualities, the standing of dharma is varied.
brahmapuran:175:26	By the influence of the qualities arise rise and fall, of holy places too, of varnas, of Vedas, of heaven and liberation.
brahmapuran:175:27	By the course of such forms, that same is distinguished; time is said to be the manifester, place the manifested.
brahmapuran:175:28	Whenever time gives manifestation, then and there that same is the manifesting, Brahmin; so there is no doubt here.
brahmapuran:175:29	The form of the gods, and the Vedic one, accords with the yuga; so too of actions, holy places, classes and stages of life.
brahmapuran:175:30	In the Satya yuga the holy place with three deities is honoured in the worlds; in another yuga with two deities; in Dvapara with one deity;
brahmapuran:175:31	in Kali nothing needs to be known. Hear another thing too: the holy place of the Krita yuga is divine, they know that of Treta as Asura,
brahmapuran:175:32	that of Dvapara is called Arsha (of sages), and in Kali it is called Manusha (human). Hear another reason too, Narada.
brahmapuran:175:33	What you asked about the Gautami I shall tell in detail: when the Ganga reached the head of Hara, great sage,
brahmapuran:175:34	from then on that Ganga became dearer to Shambhu; knowing the god's mind, Uma spoke to the elephant-faced one.
brahmapuran:175:35	Uma, queen of the three worlds, mother, benefactress of the world, peaceful, famed as Shruti, granting enjoyment and liberation:
brahmapuran:175:36	hearing his mother's word, the elephant-faced one said:
brahmapuran:175:37	What is to be done? Instruct me, mother; I shall certainly do it."
Uma, abiding in Maheshvara's matted locks, said to her son: "Ganga, dear to Isha, is to be brought down by you, truly.
Again the Lord there always stays in a wondrous way, son. Where Shiva is, there the gods and the eternal Vedas are;
there all the sages, humans and ancestors are. So turn back the Lord, the god of gods, Maheshvara.
When the god has been turned back from her, all of them will be turned back from the Ganga. Hear this word of mine: then turn Shankara back from her in every way."
Hearing his mother's words, the lord of hosts said again:

It is not possible for me to turn Shiva back from her; when Shiva is not turned back, even the gods cannot be turned back from her.
brahmapuran:175:44	They cannot be, mother of the worlds; and there is another reason: the Ganga was brought down formerly by the great-souled Gautama,
brahmapuran:175:45	the sage honoured by the world, benefactor of the three worlds, by conciliatory means at his word, worshipful through Brahmic power.
brahmapuran:175:46	Having worshipped the Lord of gods, Bhava, with austerities and hymns, the pleased Shankara said this to Gautama then:
brahmapuran:175:47	'Choose boons, holy and dear, desired in mind; whatever you wish, I shall give you all today, great-minded one.'
brahmapuran:175:48	Thus addressed by Shiva, Gautama, while I listened, said just this: 'Shankara, give me the Ganga with your matted locks; I ask for the holy Ganga; what use is another boon to me?'
brahmapuran:175:49	Shambhu, benefactor of all the worlds, said to him again:
brahmapuran:175:50	'You have asked nothing for yourself; so ask for something hard.'
brahmapuran:175:51	Gautama, not downcast, said to Bhava with joined palms:
brahmapuran:175:52	'This very thing, your sight, is hard for all; today I have obtained it by your mercy, Shankara.
brahmapuran:175:53	Even by remembrance of your feet the wise become fulfilled; what then when you, Maheshvara, are seen in person?'
brahmapuran:175:54	When Gautama had said this, Bhava, filled with joy, said, 'You asked for the benefit of the three worlds.
brahmapuran:175:55	Ask something for yourself, greatly wise one,' Shiva said to the Brahmin. Thus told, the Brahmin again reflected and said to Shiva:
brahmapuran:175:56	humbly, not downcast, full of devotion to Shiva, he again asked for the benefit of all the worlds, and while the world-guardians listened Gautama said this:
brahmapuran:175:57	'As long as the goddess flows to the sea, released from the mountain of Brahma, everywhere and always you, bull-bannered, must stay in her.
brahmapuran:175:58	You alone, lord, are the giver of fruit to the world's fruit-seekers; other holy places, lord of gods, are auspicious somewhere here and there;
brahmapuran:175:59	where your presence is constant, that they know as bestowing good; where the Ganga given by you rests in your matted crown — everywhere, by your presence, are all holy places, Shankara.'
brahmapuran:175:60	Hearing Gautama's words, Shiva again joyfully said:
brahmapuran:175:61	'Wherever, and in whatever way, whoever with devotion makes a pilgrimage, bathing, giving or libation to ancestors,
brahmapuran:175:62	hears, recites or remembers, Gautama, a man who with devotion and firm vows does so at the Godavari —
brahmapuran:175:63	the earth with seven continents, mountains, forests and groves, with jewels and herbs, lovely, with oceans, adorned with dharma —
brahmapuran:175:64	the dharma that arises from giving that, will arise from remembering the Gautami. The earth, Brahmin, is described in that way by the gift of a cow.
brahmapuran:175:65	At the time of the eclipse of the moon or sun, in my presence, with firm vows, wise, devotedly to Vishnu the supporter of the earth, at all times,
brahmapuran:175:66	one who gives beautiful cows with calves at a world-famed confluence, best of Brahmins, obtains whatever merit comes there.
brahmapuran:175:67	Greater merit than that a man obtains by bathing and giving in the Gautami, venerable to the universe, the great river, with devotion.
brahmapuran:175:68	Therefore the Godavari-Ganga brought by you will be remover of all sin and giver of all desires.'
brahmapuran:175:69	This I heard, mother, as Shiva spoke to Gautama; for this reason Shambhu stays fixed in the Ganga.
Who can turn him back, mother, the ocean of compassion? Yet, mother, let this be: humans, bound by the nooses of obstacles,
do not go to the Goda even when she is near, do not bow to the god Shiva, do not remember or praise.
So, mother, I shall do this for your satisfaction; to hold them back is a trouble; forgive my word."
From then on Vighnesha creates some obstacle for humans; one who worships him proceeds.
Then, disregarding the obstacle, he goes devotedly to the Gautami and is fulfilled in the world, with nothing left to do.
Many obstacles arise for a man, the lowest of men, who wishes to go from his house; but he who places his foot on its head and goes to the Ganga, what fruit has he not gained thereby?
Who could tell her greatness, even Sadashiva himself? It has been told by me in brief, following the story.
Whatever is the means of dharma, wealth, desire and liberation in the moving and unmoving is here in this Itihasa in detail.
This Purana, declared in the Veda, the secret of the whole Shruti, a good cause, this naming, ever well seen, was told for the world's good, joined with much dharma.
One who devoutly hears or recites a verse or even a word of this, or utters "Ganga, Ganga," obtains merit.
This Gangetic text, skilled in destroying the stains of Kali, granting all success, auspicious, benign, honoured in the world, granting the desired fruit, has been told as the best.

Well done, Gautama, may you be well; who else is like you, who obtained this Gautami Ganga and Dandakaranya?
brahmapuran:175:82	One who says 'Ganga, Ganga' even from a hundred yojanas away is freed from all sins and goes to Vishnu's world.
brahmapuran:175:83	Three and a half crore holy places in the three worlds come to bathe in the Ganga when Jupiter is in Leo.
brahmapuran:175:84	Sixty thousand years of bathing in the Bhagirathi equal a single bath in the Godavari when Jupiter is in Leo.
brahmapuran:175:85	This Gautami, son, wherever it is, by my command will give liberation to all men always from bathing.
brahmapuran:175:86	The fruit one gains from thousands of horse-sacrifices and hundreds of Vajapeyas arises from hearing this.
brahmapuran:175:87	In whose house this Purana declared by Brahma stays, there is no fear for him from the age of Kali, Narada.
brahmapuran:175:88	This excellent Purana should not be told to just anyone; it should be told to the faithful, peaceful Vaishnava, the great-souled.
brahmapuran:175:89	It is praiseworthy, giving enjoyment and liberation and destroying sin; by merely hearing it a man becomes fulfilled.
brahmapuran:175:90	One who writes this book and gives it to a Brahmin is freed from all sins and does not enter a womb again.
Having appeased the image repeatedly with bathing and gifts, Shakra, having worshipped that image, returned to his city.
Having long worshipped it with restrained speech, body and mind, he, Vritra and other cruel Asuras, headed by Namuchi,
killed those terrible Danavas and enjoyed the three worlds. When the second yuga arrived, in Treta, the lord of Rakshasas
was the very mighty, glorious Dashagriva (Ravana); without food for ten thousand years, sense-conquering,
he performed a very severe vow, supremely hard austerity; pleased by that austerity, I gave him a boon:
that he be unslayable by all gods, Daityas, serpents and Rakshasas, and unslayable by curses, fierce weapons and Yama's servants.
Having obtained the boon, that Rakshasa, having conquered the Yakshas, all these hosts and the lord of wealth, set out to conquer Shakra.
Having waged a very terrible battle with the gods, that Rakshasa defeated the king of gods, and then his son the Rakshasa Meghanada obtained the name Indrajit.
Then he reached Amaravati and the auspicious house of the king of the gods,
and the mighty Ravana saw an image of Vasudeva, dark like collyrium, endowed with all marks,
with the Shrivatsa mark, with lotus-petal eyes, a chest covered with a forest garland, adorned with crown and armlets,
with conch, discus and mace in hand, in yellow garments, four-armed, with all ornaments, granting the fruit of all desires.
Leaving the heaps of jewels, he sent the image of auspicious marks quickly to Lanka on the Pushpaka vehicle.
The glorious, righteous Vibhishana was the city's overseer, Ravana's younger brother and minister, devoted to Narayana.
Seeing that divine image fallen from the palace of the lord of gods, with hair standing on end, he was filled with wonder.
Bowing his head to the god, with a delighted heart: "Today my birth is fruitful, today my austerity is fruitful."
Having said so, the righteous one bowed again and again, approached his elder brother and said with joined palms:
King, you ought to show me favour with the image, by worshipping which, lord of the world, I may cross the ocean of existence.
Hearing his brother's words, Ravana then said to him: "Take the image, hero; what shall I do with it?
I shall conquer the three worlds by worshipping the Self-born; this god is full of many wonders, the source of the origin of all beings."
The greatly wise Vibhishana, having worshipped Janardana in that auspicious image for one hundred and eight years,
attained freedom from old age and death, endowed with the qualities such as anima; he enjoys kingship and lordship of Lanka and the pleasures he wants.

Ah, wonder has arisen in us on hearing this supreme nectar: the rare birth of the infinite Vasudeva on earth.
brahmapuran:176:36	We wish to hear, god, in detail as it was; you ought to tell the greatness of that god fully.
Then that cruel Rakshasa, the sinner, having conquered in battle gods, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, world-guardians, humans, sages and Siddhas,
took away their women and, establishing the city of Lanka, again bewildered for Sita's sake,
Ravana, suspicious of the golden deer form, then — angry Rama with Lakshmana in battle,
for the slaying of Ravana, having killed Vali (swift as mind), Sugriva was consecrated and Angada as crown prince,
Hanuman, Nala, Nila, Jambavan, Panasa, Gavaya, Gavaksha and the supremely mighty Pathina:
surrounded by these and many other very mighty monkeys, Rama, lotus-eyed, with a terrible host,
building a bridge in the great ocean with masses of mountains, crossed the great ocean with a great force
and fought an incomparable battle with the Rakshasa hosts. The valiant Rama killed Prahasta, Nikumbha and Kumbha,
the greatly mighty Narantaka, likewise Yamantaka, Malyavan and Malika.
Again, having killed Indrajit, Kumbhakarna and Ravana, purifying Vaidehi by fire and giving the kingdom to Vibhishana,
taking Vasudeva (the image) he mounted the Pushpaka vehicle and easily reached Ayodhya, formerly ruled by him.
Then Rama, kind to devotees, consecrated his younger brother Bharata and Shatrughna out of affection, as supreme sovereign over all kingdoms.
Worshipping the ancient image of himself, Hari, for ten thousand and ten hundred years
Raghava enjoyed the earth to the ocean's edge; attaining kingdom, he entered the Vaishnava state, the good goal.
And that image Rama gave to the Lord of the sea: "Blessed, you will guard it, you endowed with jewels of the waters."
When the god, lord of the world, reached the Dvapara yuga, at the request of the earth and because of laxity of mind,
the revered lord was born in the family of Vasudeva to slay Kamsa and others, with Sankarshana as helper.
Then that image, Brahmins, granting the fruit of all wishes, for the benefit of all the worlds, for some other reason,
in that excellent holy field, the rare Purushottama, Ocean, lord of rivers, himself lifted out of the water.
From then on in that very field granting liberation, Brahmins, the god abides, granting the fruit of all desires to the gods.
Those who with devotion constantly take refuge in the Infinite, the lord of all, by speech, mind and action, go to the supreme state.
One who has once seen Ananta with devotion, worshipped and bowed, obtains tenfold the fruit of the Rajasuya and the horse-sacrifice.
In a sun-coloured vehicle going where he wills, abundant in all desires, radiant, wreathed with nets of little bells,
having lifted twenty-one generations, served by hosts of divine women, sung to by Gandharvas, a man goes to Vishnu's city.
Having enjoyed excellent pleasures there, free of old age and death, bearing a divine form, glorious, until the dissolution of beings,
when merit is exhausted he comes here as a four-Veda Brahmin and, taking up Vaishnava yoga, attains liberation.
Thus Ananta has been described by me, best of sages; who can tell his virtues even in hundreds of years?
Because he is beyond Prakriti and also higher than Purusha, therefore in the Veda, the Purana and in this world he is Purushottama.
He who is called the Supreme Self in the Purana and Vedanta abides for the benefit of the world; therefore he is Purushottama.
On a road, in a cremation ground, in a house-hall or even on streets, wherever a man gives up his body, wishing or not wishing, he obtains liberation.
Therefore with all effort, best of Brahmins, men desiring liberation should give up the body in that field properly.
The greatness of the one called Purusha has not been and will not be; where a man abandons his body he attains rare liberation.
Only a part of the virtues of that field has been told by me; who can tell all its virtues even in hundreds of years?
If you, best of sages, desire eternal liberation, live unweariedly in that excellent holy field.
Hearing the words of Brahma, of unmanifest birth, they made their dwelling there and obtained the supreme state.
Therefore you, with effort, best of Brahmins, should live in the excellent field called Purusha if you desire liberation.
Going there she saw a lovely excellent forest and a sage of blazing austerity in his hermitage, faultless.
She saw with them the lovely forest, like Nandana, rich in excellent flowers of all seasons, thronged with troops of monkeys,
holy, with lotus-like strength, with shoots and great strength, with sweet sounds delightful to the ear uttered by the mouths of birds,
and trees laden with fruit of all seasons, bright with flowers of all seasons, resounding with birds.
She saw mango, amrataka, bhavya, coconut with satindu, then bilva, jiva, pomegranate and citron,
jackfruit, lakucha, nipa, shirisha, charming, pigeons, kola, arimeda, amlavetasa,
bhallataka, amalaka, shataparna, kimshuka, ingudi, karavira, haritaki and vibhitaki.
The broad-eyed one saw these and other trees, and likewise ashoka, punnaga, ketaki and bakula,
parijata, kovidara, mandara, indivara, blossoming lovely patala trees and deodar trees.
